title: On Keeping
summary: On the keeping of things. — from the Ollery bequest

pages.text: Cut on the slant, dip in the wax {~and speak the date~}. The bloom keeps {~a season~}, colour and all.
For books and letters: a breath of {?tessel-dust?} {~between the leaves~}, and the damp {~turns away~}.
Bread, cheese and apples keep {~past their season~} under a cloth so charmed.
What this touches stops. {~Not sleeps; stops.~} {~It does not ask~} whether {~a thing~} is living.
pages.authorNote: Outlier. Shares eye of newt and beeswax with Hold Fast. Osric's accident.

pages.text: A case so lined keeps what is in it {~as it was put in~}. {~Lock it.~}
